claim: Cellular growth is the result of passive physical constraints and active biological processes.
source: Cellular growth is the result of passive physical constraints and active biological processes.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that frames the study's approach.

claim: The interplay of passive physical constraints and active biological processes leads to the appearance of robust and ubiquitous scaling laws relating linearly cell size, dry mass, and nuclear size.
source: Their interplay leads to the appearance of robust and ubiquitous scaling laws relating linearly cell size, dry mass, and nuclear size.
evidence: This statement is supported by the theoretical framework and experimental comparisons presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The scaling laws relating cell size, dry mass, and nuclear size can be explained quantitatively by a single model of size regulation based on three simple, yet generic, physical constraints defining the Pump-Leak model.
source: Here, we show that these laws can be explained quantitatively by a single model of size regulation based on three simple, yet generic, physical constraints defining altogether the Pump-Leak model.
evidence: The manuscript presents theoretical derivations and quantitative comparisons with experimental data to support this claim.

claim: Dry mass density homeostasis arises from the scaling between proteins and small osmolytes, mainly amino acids and ions.
source: We propose that dry mass density homeostasis arises from the scaling between proteins and small osmolytes, mainly amino acids and ions.
evidence: This is supported by the theoretical model and order of magnitude estimates presented in the manuscript.

claim: The model predicts that dry mass density homeostasis naturally fails at senescence when DNA and RNAs are saturated by RNA polymerases and ribosomes, respectively.
source: Our model predicts this scaling to naturally fail, both at senescence when DNA and RNAs are saturated by RNA polymerases and ribosomes, respectively, and at mitotic entry due to the counterion release following histone tail modifications.
evidence: This prediction is tested quantitatively using published data from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: The model predicts that dry mass density homeostasis naturally fails at mitotic entry due to counterion release following histone tail modifications.
source: Our model predicts this scaling to naturally fail, both at senescence when DNA and RNAs are saturated by RNA polymerases and ribosomes, respectively, and at mitotic entry due to the counterion release following histone tail modifications.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on polymer physics and the Pump-Leak model.

claim: Nuclear scaling results from osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope and a large pool of metabolites, which dilutes chromatin counterions that do not scale during growth.
source: Based on the same physical laws, we further show that nuclear scaling results from a osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope and a large pool of metabolites, which dilutes chromatin counterions that do not scale during growth.
evidence: This is supported by the nested Pump-Leak model and numerical simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Each cell type often shows small volumetric variance at a given stage of its cycle.
source: Although cell size varies dramatically between cell types, during the cell cycle, and depends on various external stresses (Cadart et al., 2019), each cell type often shows small volumetric variance at a given stage of its cycle.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cadart et al., 2019.

claim: Tight control of cell size reflects the importance of size in monitoring cell function.
source: This tight control reflects the importance of size in monitoring cell function.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established biological knowledge.

claim: Generic linear scaling relations exist between cell volume, cell dry mass, and the volume of the nucleus.
source: It is often associated to generic linear scaling relations between cell volume, cell dry mass, and the volume of the nucleus (Neurohr and Amon, 2020; Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b; Webster et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: These scaling laws have fascinated biologists for more than a century.
source: These scaling laws have fascinated biologists for more than a century (Wilson, 1925; Conklin, 1912) because of the inherent biological complexity and their ubiquity both in yeasts, bacteria, and mammals, hence raising the question of the underlying physical laws.
evidence: This is supported by historical citations to Wilson, 1925 and Conklin, 1912.

claim: Scaling laws are ubiquitous in yeasts, bacteria, and mammals.
source: These scaling laws have fascinated biologists for more than a century (Wilson, 1925; Conklin, 1912) because of the inherent biological complexity and their ubiquity both in yeasts, bacteria, and mammals, hence raising the question of the underlying physical laws.
evidence: This is supported by citations and is a well-established observation in biology.

claim: Scaling relations break down in a host of pathologies.
source: Although robust, these scaling relations do break down in a host of pathologies.
evidence: This is supported by subsequent examples and citations in the manuscript.

claim: The nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (NC) ratio has long been used by pathologists to diagnose and stage cancers.
source: The nuclear-to-cytoplasmic (NC) ratio (also called karyoplasmic ratio) has long been used by pathologists to diagnose and stage cancers (Jevtić and Levy, 2014; Slater et al., 2005; Zink et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Senescent cells such as fibroblasts are known to be swollen and their dry mass diluted.
source: Similarly, senescent cells such as fibroblasts are known to be swollen and their dry mass diluted (Neurohr et al., 2019), a feature suspected to be of fundamental biological importance since it could represent a determinant of stem cell potential during ageing (Lengefeld et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Neurohr et al., 2019 and Lengefeld et al., 2021.

claim: Dry mass dilution in senescent cells could represent a determinant of stem cell potential during ageing.
source: Similarly, senescent cells such as fibroblasts are known to be swollen and their dry mass diluted (Neurohr et al., 2019), a feature suspected to be of fundamental biological importance since it could represent a determinant of stem cell potential during ageing (Lengefeld et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Lengefeld et al., 2021.

claim: The principles ruling cell size, growth, and associated scaling laws have not yet been fully resolved.
source: Paradoxically, although cells are the simplest building blocks of living organisms, the principles ruling their size, their growth, and the associated scaling laws have not yet been fully resolved.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field.

claim: Experimental difficulty in performing accurate volume and dry mass measurements contributes to the lack of resolution of principles ruling cell size.
source: This is in part due to the experimental difficulty to perform accurate volume and dry mass measurements (Model, 2018; Cadart et al., 2017; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Many methods for measuring cell volume and dry mass were developed in the past decades, but they sometimes lead to contradictory observations.
source: Many methods were developed in the past decades, but they sometimes lead to contradictory observations, highlighting the need of comparing and benchmarking each method (Guo et al., 2017; Venkova et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2017 and Venkova et al., 2022.

claim: Extensive experimental investigations have identified a plethora of biological features influencing cell size scalings.
source: Moreover, extensive experimental investigations have identified a plethora of biological features influencing these scalings (Lang et al., 1998; Hoffmann et al., 2009) but comparatively fewer theoretical studies have precisely addressed them, leaving many experimental data unrelated and unexplained.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lang et al., 1998 and Hoffmann et al., 2009.

claim: Comparatively fewer theoretical studies have precisely addressed cell size scalings, leaving many experimental data unrelated and unexplained.
source: Moreover, extensive experimental investigations have identified a plethora of biological features influencing these scalings (Lang et al., 1998; Hoffmann et al., 2009) but comparatively fewer theoretical studies have precisely addressed them, leaving many experimental data unrelated and unexplained.
evidence: This is a general observation about the state of the field.

claim: The 'nucleoskeletal theory' emphasizes the role of DNA content in controlling the NC ratio based on the idea that ploidy dictates cell and nuclear sizes.
source: The 'nucleoskeletal theory' emphasizes the role of the DNA content in controlling the NC ratio based on the idea that ploidy dictates cell and nuclear sizes since tetraploid cells tend to be larger than their diploid homologs (Webster et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a description of an existing theory supported by a citation to Webster et al., 2009.

claim: Tetraploid cells tend to be larger than their diploid homologs.
source: The 'nucleoskeletal theory' emphasizes the role of the DNA content in controlling the NC ratio based on the idea that ploidy dictates cell and nuclear sizes since tetraploid cells tend to be larger than their diploid homologs (Webster et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an empirical observation cited from Webster et al., 2009.

claim: Genome size is not the only determining factor for nuclear size.
source: Other experiments suggest that genome size is not the only determining factor: indeed it would not explain why cells from different tissues, having the same amount of DNA, have different sizes.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental observations.

claim: Nuclear size depends on cytoplasmic content, nucleo-cytoplasmic transport, transcription, RNA processing, and mechanics of nuclear envelope structural elements such as lamina.
source: Instead, it has been shown that nuclear size depends on cytoplasmic content, nucleo-cytoplasmic transport, transcription, RNA processing, and mechanics of nuclear envelope structural elements such as lamina (Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b.

claim: Theoretical models based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics were developed to understand cell size.
source: In parallel, theoretical models, based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, were developed (Kedem and Katchalsky, 1958; Mori, 2012; Marbach and Bocquet, 2019), often based on the 'Pump-Leak' principle (Cadart et al., 2019; Venkova et al., 2022; Adar and Safran, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Charged impermeant molecules in cells create an imbalance of osmotic pressure at the origin of the Donnan effect.
source: Charged impermeant molecules in cells create an imbalance of osmotic pressure at the origin of the so-called Donnan effect (Sten-Knudsen, 2007).
evidence: This is a well-established physical principle supported by a citation.

claim: Cells have two main ways to counteract osmotic imbalance: adapting to sustain high hydrostatic pressure difference (like plants) or using ion pumps to actively decrease the number of ions inside the cells (like mammalian cells).
source: Cells have two main ways to counteract the osmotic imbalance. They can adapt to sustain a high hydrostatic pressure difference as plants do by building cellulose walls. Or, as done by mammalian cells, they can use ion pumps to actively decrease the number of ions inside the cells, thus decreasing the osmotic pressure difference across the cell membrane and therefore impeding water penetration.
evidence: This is based on established biological knowledge.

claim: There is poor understanding of the correspondence between biological factors and physical parameters of the Pump-Leak model.
source: However, due to the large number of parameters of these models, we still have a poor understanding of the correspondence between biological factors and physical parameters of the model.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of the field that motivates the current study.

claim: The dry mass of the cell is dominated by the contribution of proteins.
source: We find that the dry mass of the cell is dominated by the contribution of the proteins, while the cell volume is mostly fixed by the contribution to the osmotic pressure of small osmolytes, such as amino acids and ions.
evidence: This is supported by order of magnitude estimates presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The cell volume is mostly fixed by the contribution to the osmotic pressure of small osmolytes, such as amino acids and ions.
source: We find that the dry mass of the cell is dominated by the contribution of the proteins, while the cell volume is mostly fixed by the contribution to the osmotic pressure of small osmolytes, such as amino acids and ions.
evidence: This is supported by order of magnitude estimates presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The maintenance of homeostatic cell density during growth is due to a linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers.
source: The maintenance of a homeostatic cell density during growth is then due to a linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion derived from the Pump-Leak model and growth model.

claim: The linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers is obtained in the exponential growth regime of the cell by virtue of the enzymatic control of amino acid production.
source: Combining simplified models of gene transcription and translation and of amino acid biosynthesis to the Pump-Leak model, we show that the linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers is obtained in the exponential growth regime of the cell by virtue of the enzymatic control of amino acid production.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on the combined models presented in the manuscript.

claim: The absence of linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers is at the root of the breakdown of density homeostasis.
source: On the other hand, the absence of linear scaling relation between protein and small osmolyte numbers is at the root of the breakdown of density homeostasis.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion derived from the model.

claim: The change of mechanical tension at the plasma membrane during cell spreading alters the permeability of ion channels and results in a volume adaptation at constant dry mass.
source: Recent studies Venkova et al., 2022; Adar and Safran, 2020 have indeed shown that the change of mechanical tension at the plasma membrane during cell spreading alters the permeability of ion channels and results in a volume adaptation at constant dry mass.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Venkova et al., 2022 and Adar and Safran, 2020.

claim: The synthesis of glycerol occurs in budding yeast following a hypertonic shock.
source: Another important way through which cells control their size independently of their mass is through metabolite synthesis. An example is the synthesis of glycerol that occurs in budding yeast following a hypertonic shock (Neurohr and Amon, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Neurohr and Amon, 2020.

claim: At senescence, DNA and RNAs become saturated by RNA polymerases and ribosomes, respectively, leading to a change of the growth regime where protein number saturates while amino acid number increases linearly with time.
source: At senescence, cells cannot divide properly. Our theory then predicts that DNA and RNAs become saturated by RNA polymerases (RNAPs) and ribosomes, respectively, leading to a change of the growth regime: the protein number saturates while the amino acid number increases linearly with time, resulting in the experimentally observed dry mass dilution.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction tested against published data from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: At mitotic entry, chromatin rearrangements such as histone tail modifications induce a counterion release inside the cell, resulting in an influx of water and dry mass dilution.
source: At mitotic entry, chromatin rearrangements, such as histone tail modifications, induce a counterion release inside the cell, resulting in an influx of water and dry mass dilution in order to maintain the osmotic balance at the cell membrane.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on polymer physics and the Pump-Leak model.

claim: Nuclear scaling requires osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope.
source: Using a nested Pump-Leak model for the cell and for the nucleus, we show that nuclear scaling requires osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion from the nested Pump-Leak model.

claim: The osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope is explained by the nonlinear osmotic response of mammalian nuclei attributed to the presence of folds at the surface of many nuclei.
source: The osmotic balance is explained by the nonlinear osmotic response of mammalian nuclei that we attribute to the presence of folds at the surface of many nuclei (Lomakin et al., 2020), which in turn buffer the nuclear envelope tension and enforce scaling.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation supported by a citation to Lomakin et al., 2020.

claim: Metabolites play an essential role in the NC ratio despite being permeable to the nuclear envelope.
source: Counterintuitively, metabolites, though permeable to the nuclear envelope, are predicted to play an essential role in the NC ratio.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the nested Pump-Leak model.

claim: High concentrations of metabolites in cells is a conserved feature throughout living cells.
source: Their high concentrations in cells, a conserved feature throughout living cells, is shown to dilute the chromatin counterions that do not scale during growth, thereby allowing the scaling of nuclear size with cell size both at the population level and during individual cell growth.
evidence: This is based on established biological knowledge and data from Park et al., 2016.

claim: The Pump-Leak model is a coarse-grained model emphasizing the role of mechanical and osmotic balance.
source: The Pump-Leak model is a coarse-grained model emphasizing the role of mechanical and osmotic balance.
evidence: This is a description of the theoretical framework used in the study.

claim: The osmotic balance involves two types of osmolytes: impermeant molecules such as proteins and metabolites, and ions which cross the cell membrane.
source: The osmotic balance involves two types of osmolytes, impermeant molecules such as proteins and metabolites, which cannot diffuse through the cell membrane, and ions, which cross the cell membrane and for which at steady state the incoming flux into the cell must equate the outgoing flux.
evidence: This is a description of the model components.

claim: In the Pump-Leak model, only cations are pumped outward of the cell.
source: For simplicity, we restrict ourselves to a two-ion Pump-Leak model where only cations are pumped outward of the cell.
evidence: This is a simplifying assumption of the model justified in the Discussion.

claim: The laws of electrostatics ensure that in any aqueous solution such as the cytoplasm, the solution is neutral at length scales larger than the Debye screening length.
source: Electroneutrality: the laws of electrostatics ensure that in any aqueous solution such as the cytoplasm, the solution is neutral at length scales larger than the Debye screening length, that is, the electrostatic charge of any volume larger than the screening length vanishes.
evidence: This is a fundamental principle of electrostatics.

claim: In physiological conditions, the Debye screening length is typically on the nanometric scale.
source: In physiological conditions, the screening length is typically on the nanometric scale.
evidence: This is established physical knowledge about electrostatic screening in biological systems.

claim: The timescale to reach the equilibrium of water is of few seconds after a perturbation.
source: Osmotic balance: balance of the chemical potential of water inside and outside the cell; the timescale to reach the equilibrium of water is of few seconds after a perturbation (Venkova et al., 2022; Milo and Phillips, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Venkova et al., 2022 and Milo and Phillips, 2015.

claim: The typical timescales of ion relaxation observed during a cell regulatory volume response after an osmotic shock are of the order of a few minutes.
source: Balance of ionic fluxes: the typical timescales of ion relaxation observed during a cell regulatory volume response after an osmotic shock are of the order of a few minutes (Venkova et al., 2022; Hoffmann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Venkova et al., 2022 and Hoffmann et al., 2009.

claim: The quasi-static theory is designed to study cell volume variations on timescales larger than a few minutes.
source: Together, this means that our quasi-static theory is designed to study cell volume variations on timescales larger than a few minutes.
evidence: This is a logical conclusion from the timescales of water and ion equilibration.

claim: Osmotic pressure is balanced at the plasma membrane of a mammalian cell since hydrostatic and osmotic pressures differ by at least three orders of magnitude.
source: (2) Osmotic pressure is balanced at the plasma membrane of a mammalian cell since hydrostatic and osmotic pressures differ by at least three orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is based on order of magnitude estimates presented in Table 1.

claim: Metabolites and their counterions account for most of the wet volume of the cell, 78% of the wet volume against 1% for proteins.
source: Metabolites and their counterions account for most of the wet volume of the cell, 78% of the wet volume against 1% for proteins.
evidence: This is based on order of magnitude estimates and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Proteins account for most of the dry mass of mammalian cells, accounting for 60% of the cellular dry mass against 17% for metabolites.
source: On the other hand, proteins account for most of the dry mass of mammalian cells, accounting for 60% of the cellular dry mass against 17% for metabolites.
evidence: This is based on order of magnitude estimates and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Metabolites are mainly amino acids, and in particular three of them, glutamate, glutamine, and aspartate, account for 73% of the metabolites.
source: We further note that metabolites are mainly amino acids and in particular three of them, glutamate, glutamine, and aspartate, account for 73% of the metabolites (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Park et al., 2016.

claim: The relative proportion of free amino acids in the cell does not follow their relative proportion in the composition of proteins.
source: It is important to note that the relative proportion of free amino acids in the cell does not follow their relative proportion in the composition of proteins.
evidence: This is supported by specific examples comparing glutamate proportions.

claim: Glutamate represents 50% of the free amino acid pool while its relative appearance in proteins is only 6%.
source: For instance, glutamate represents 50% of the free amino acid pool while its relative appearance in proteins is only 6% (King and Jukes, 1969).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to King and Jukes, 1969.

claim: Some amino acids have roles other than building up proteins.
source: This is evidence that some amino acids have other roles than building up proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the disproportionate representation of certain amino acids in the free pool versus in proteins.

claim: The model predicts that the saturation of DNA precedes that of mRNAs.
source: Note that the model predicts that the saturation of DNA precedes that of mRNAs, whose number initially increases with the number of RNAPs (Equation 8) while the number of genes remains constant.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the growth model.

claim: The homeostasis of dry mass density naturally breaks down if the time spent in the G1 phase is too long.
source: Not only does our model explain the homeostasis of the dry mass, but it also makes the salient prediction that this homeostasis naturally breaks down if the time spent in the G1 phase is too long.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: In the saturated regime, the number of amino acids increases linearly with time while the number of proteins saturates, leading to volume growing linearly with time and dry mass dilution.
source: In this regime, the volume thus grows linearly with time but the dry mass remains constant, leading to its dilution and the decrease in the dry mass density (see Appendix 1, section 4.1 and Equation A.45):
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: The growth rate in the linear regime scales with the ploidy of the cell, as opposed to the growth rate in the exponential regime.
source: Second, the growth rate in the linear regime scales with the ploidy of the cell, as opposed to the growth rate in the exponential regime.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Two distinct growth regimes are observed in the volume data of nondividing yeast cells: an initial exponential growth followed by a linear growth.
source: Two distinct growth regimes are observed, at least on the population level, in the volume data of nondividing yeast cells (Neurohr et al., 2019) an initial exponential growth followed by a linear growth (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 2C and cited from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: Cells treated with rapamycin exhibit both a constant protein content and a linear volume increase during the whole growth.
source: Our theory also predicts that as long as protein number is constant the volume must grow linearly (Equations 9 and A.45). This is precisely what is observed in the experiments: cells treated with rapamycin exhibit both a constant protein content and a linear volume increase during the whole growth (see Figure S6.F in Neurohr et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data cited from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: The typical time to reach the linear growth regime is of the order of 3 hr and seems independent of the ploidy of the cell.
source: Indeed, while the typical time to reach the linear growth regime – of the order of 3 hr – seems independent of the ploidy of the cell, the volume at which dilution occurs is doubled (see Figure S7.A in Neurohr et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data cited from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: The volume at which dilution occurs is doubled for diploid cells compared to haploid cells.
source: Indeed, while the typical time to reach the linear growth regime – of the order of 3 hr – seems independent of the ploidy of the cell, the volume at which dilution occurs is doubled (see Figure S7.A in Neurohr et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data cited from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: The growth rate during the linear regime scales with ploidy: haploid cells have a growth rate of order 129 fL/h against 270 fL/h for their diploid counterparts.
source: Moreover, the growth rate during the linear regime scales with ploidy as the haploid cells growth rate is of order 129fL/h against 270fL/h for their diploid counterparts (Neurohr et al., 2019).
evidence: This is data from Neurohr et al., 2019.

claim: The dilution of cellular dry mass at senescence originates from the physical crowding of mRNAs by ribosomes without invoking any genetic response of the cell.
source: In summary, our theoretical framework combining the Pump-Leak model with a growth model and a model of amino acid biosynthesis provides a consistent quantitative description of the dry mass density homeostasis and its subsequent dilution at senescence without invoking any genetic response of the cell; the dilution is due to the physical crowding of mRNAs by ribosomes.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion from the combined models.

claim: Mitotic swelling or mitotic overshoot is believed to play a key role in the change of the physicochemical properties of mitotic cells.
source: Although this so-called mitotic swelling or mitotic overshoot is believed to play a key role in the change of the physicochemical properties of mitotic cells, its origin remains unclear (Son et al., 2015; Zlotek-Zlotkiewicz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the biological significance of mitotic swelling supported by citations.

claim: Mitotic swelling originates from an influx of water happening between prophase and metaphase, resulting in a typical 10% volume increase in cells.
source: (1) It originates from an influx of water happening between prophase and metaphase, resulting in a typical 10% volume increase in the cells.
evidence: This is an established observation about mitotic swelling.

claim: Mitotic swelling is reversible and cells shrink back to their initial volume between anaphase and telophase.
source: (2) The swelling is reversible and cells shrink back to their initial volume between anaphase and telophase.
evidence: This is an established observation about mitotic swelling.

claim: Mitotic swelling appears to be universal to mammalian cells, with larger cells displaying larger swellings.
source: (3) This phenomenon appears to be universal to mammalian cells, larger cells displaying larger swellings.
evidence: This is an established observation about mitotic swelling.

claim: Cortical actin is not involved in mitotic swelling, discarding a possible involvement of the mechanosensitivity of ion channels.
source: (4) Cortical actin was shown not to be involved in the process, discarding a possible involvement of the mechanosensitivity of ion channels, contrary to the density increase observed during cell spreading (Venkova et al., 2022)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Venkova et al., 2022.

claim: Nuclear envelope breakdown (NEB) alone cannot explain the mitotic overshoot since most of the swelling is observed before the prometaphase where NEB occurs.
source: (5) Nuclear envelope breakdown (NEB) alone cannot explain the mitotic overshoot since most of the swelling is observed before the prometaphase where NEB occurs (Son et al., 2015; Zlotek-Zlotkiewicz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Son et al., 2015 and Zlotek-Zlotkiewicz et al., 2015.

claim: Counterion condensation is a well-known electrostatic property of charged polymers first studied by Manning, 1969.
source: We show how every feature of the mitotic overshoot can be qualitatively explained by our theory, based on a well-known electrostatic property of charged polymer called counterion condensation first studied by Manning, 1969.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Manning, 1969.

claim: Condensed counterions do not contribute to the osmotic pressure.
source: The condensed counterions then do not contribute to the osmotic pressure given by Equation 2, which determines the cell volume.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion about the role of condensed counterions.

claim: A release of condensed counterions increases the number of free cellular osmolytes and thus the osmotic pressure inside the cell, leading to an influx of water.
source: A release of condensed counterions increases the number of free cellular osmolytes and thus the osmotic pressure inside the cell. Therefore, it would lead to an influx of water in order to restore osmotic balance at the plasma membrane (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on the Pump-Leak model and illustrated in Figure 3.

claim: Chromatin undergoes large conformational changes at mitotic entry.
source: Biologists have shown that chromatin undergoes large conformational changes at mitotic entry.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: The affinity between DNA and histones is enhanced during chromatin compaction by stronger electrostatic interactions thanks to specific covalent modifications of histone tails by enzymes.
source: It is widely accepted that the affinity between DNA and histones is enhanced during chromatin compaction by stronger electrostatic interactions thanks to specific covalent modifications of histone tails by enzymes.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge cited from Alberts et al., 2002.

claim: Some histone tail modifications such as the deacetylation of lysines add a positive charge to the histone tails, making the chromatin less negatively charged.
source: Some of these modifications such as the deacetylation of lysines add a positive charge to the histone tails, hence making the chromatin less negatively charged (Alberts et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge cited from Alberts et al., 2002.

claim: Histone tails are massively deacetylated during chromatin compaction.
source: Moreover, histone tails are massively deacetylated during chromatin compaction (Zhiteneva et al., 2017), potentially meaning that this specific reaction plays an important role in counterion release and thus on the observed mitotic swelling.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhiteneva et al., 2017.

claim: Chromatin counterion release can explain the amplitude of mitotic swelling.
source: Admittedly crude, this estimate suggests that chromatin counterion release can indeed explain the amplitude of mitotic swelling.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion based on the order of magnitude estimate.

claim: All mammalian cells swell during prophase and shrink during chromatin decondensation after anaphase.
source: In brief, the decondensation of the chromatin condensed counterions, hypothetically due to histone tail modifications, is sufficient to induce a 10% swelling. This implies that all mammalian cells swell during prophase and shrink during chromatin decondensation after anaphase; again, consistent with the dynamics of the mitotic overshoot observed on many cell types.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction consistent with experimental observations.

claim: The amplitude of mitotic swelling is positively correlated with the genome content of the cells.
source: Another salient implication is that the amplitude of the swelling is positively correlated with the genome content of the cells: cells having more chromatin are also expected to possess a larger 'internal reservoir' of osmolytes, which can participate in decondensation.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Hela cells swell on average by 20%, in agreement with the fact that many of them are tetraploid.
source: For instance, Hela cells were shown to swell on average by 20%, in agreement with the fact that many of them are tetraploid.
evidence: This is an observation that supports the theoretical prediction.

claim: The volume of cell organelles is proportional to cell volume.
source: Another widely documented scaling law related to cell volume states that the volume of cell organelles is proportional to cell volume (Chan and Marshall, 2010; Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chan and Marshall, 2010 and Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b.

claim: The osmotic balance at the nuclear envelope leads to a linear scaling relation between the volumes of the nucleus and cytoplasm.
source: In addition, a crucial consequence of the osmotic balance condition at the nuclear envelope is that it leads to a linear scaling relation between the volumes of the two compartments:
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion from the nested Pump-Leak model (Equation 12).

claim: The linear scaling between the nucleus and the cytoplasm has been reported repeatedly over the last century and is known as nuclear scaling.
source: Importantly, this linear scaling between the nucleus and the cytoplasm was reported repeatedly over the last century and is known as nuclear scaling (Webster et al., 2009; Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Webster et al., 2009 and Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b.

claim: The NC ratio would be four times larger in the absence of metabolites.
source: As a key consequence, we find that the NC ratio would be four times larger in the absence of metabolites (see Appendix 1—figure 1B).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction shown in Appendix 1—figure 1B.

claim: Variations of the NC ratio and variations of the nuclear envelope potential are strongly correlated.
source: Interestingly, variations of the NC ratio and variations of the nuclear envelope potential are strongly correlated, a feature that can be tested experimentally (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In order to maintain a constant NC ratio during the cell cycle, cells must contain a large pool of metabolites.
source: Moreover, we deduce from our numerical results that, in order to maintain a constant NC ratio during the cell cycle, cells must contain a large pool of metabolites (see Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The regime of large metabolite pool is genuinely the biological regime throughout biology, providing a natural explanation on the origin of the nuclear scaling.
source: Our estimates point out that this regime is genuinely the biological regime throughout biology, thus providing a natural explanation on the origin of the nuclear scaling.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion based on order of magnitude estimates.

claim: Good metabolic targets for experiments to test the role of metabolites on NC ratio could be glutamate or glutamine because they account for a large proportion of the metabolites in the cell.
source: Importantly, good metabolic targets in these experiments could be glutamate or glutamine because they account for a large proportion of the metabolites in the cell (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a suggestion based on data from Park et al., 2016.

claim: Cells with a smaller metabolic pool are expected to experience higher variations of the NC ratio during growth and thus larger fluctuations of this ratio at the population level.
source: We also point out that cells with a smaller metabolic pool are expected to experience higher variations of the NC ratio during growth and thus larger fluctuations of this ratio at the population level (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Metabolic reprogramming is being recognized as a hallmark of cancer.
source: Indeed, metabolic reprogramming is being recognized as a hallmark of cancer (Fujita et al., 2020) some cancer cells increase their consumption of the pool of glutamate and glutamine to fuel the TCA cycle and enhance their proliferation and invasiveness (Altman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fujita et al., 2020 and Altman et al., 2016.

claim: Some cancer cells increase their consumption of the pool of glutamate and glutamine to fuel the TCA cycle and enhance their proliferation and invasiveness.
source: Indeed, metabolic reprogramming is being recognized as a hallmark of cancer (Fujita et al., 2020) some cancer cells increase their consumption of the pool of glutamate and glutamine to fuel the TCA cycle and enhance their proliferation and invasiveness (Altman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Altman et al., 2016.

claim: Disruption of nuclear import leads to a natural decrease of the NC ratio.
source: Numerical solutions of the equations displayed in Appendix 1—figure 1 show a natural decrease of the NC ratio due to the disruption of nuclear import.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from numerical solutions shown in Appendix 1—figure 1.

claim: If nuclear export is disrupted, an increase in the NC ratio is expected.
source: On the other hand, if nuclear export is disrupted, we expect an increase in the NC ratio.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Experiments blocking nuclear export show a transient decrease followed by an increase in diffusivities in the nucleus.
source: This is in agreement with experiments done recently in yeast cells (Lemière et al., 2022). The authors reported a transient decrease followed by an increase in the diffusivities in the nucleus.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lemière et al., 2022.

claim: Changing the external ion concentration does not influence nuclear scaling directly as long as the nuclear envelope is not under strong tension.
source: Finally, our framework also predicts that experiments that would maintain the five essential parameters unchanged would preserve the nuclear scaling. We thus expect that, as long as the nuclear envelope is not under strong tension, changing the external ion concentration does not influence the scaling directly.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Experiments show that changing external ion concentration does not influence nuclear scaling, consistent with the model prediction.
source: Experiments already published in the literature (Guo et al., 2017) show precisely this feature.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guo et al., 2017.

claim: Small nuclear envelope extensions of 10% would be sufficient to impact nuclear volume assuming linear elasticity.
source: (3) Assuming linear elasticity, small nuclear envelope extensions of 10% would be sufficient to impact nuclear volume.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion based on order of magnitude estimates.

claim: The constitutive equation for the tension in the lamina is nonlinear, likely originating from the folds and wrinkles that many nuclei exhibit.
source: These conclusions stand in stark contrast to the observed robustness of the nuclear scaling, thus pointing out that the constitutive equation for the tension in the lamina is nonlinear. Biologically, we postulate that this nonlinearity originates from the folds and wrinkles that many nuclei exhibit (Lomakin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation supported by a citation to Lomakin et al., 2020.

claim: Nuclear folds could play the effective role of membrane reservoirs, preventing the nuclear envelope tension to grow with the nuclear volume.
source: These folds could indeed play the effective role of membrane reservoirs, preventing the nuclear envelope tension to grow with the nuclear volume, hence setting the nuclear pressure difference to a small constant value, and maintaining cells in the scaling regime discussed in the previous sections.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation.

claim: The nucleus exhibits nonlinear osmotic properties.
source: This conclusion is consistent with the results of Finan et al., 2009, which observed that the nucleus exhibits nonlinear osmotic properties.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Finan et al., 2009.

claim: Chromatin plays a negligible role on nuclear mechanics for moderate extensions.
source: For simplicity, we ignore the mechanical contribution of chromatin that was shown to play a negligible role on nuclear mechanics for moderate extensions (Stephens et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Stephens et al., 2017.

claim: The saturation of the nuclear volume under strong hypo-osmotic shock originates from the pressure build up in the nucleus after the unfolding of the folds, implying a significant decrease in the NC ratio and a loss of nuclear scaling.
source: The saturation of the nuclear volume under strong hypo-osmotic shock originating from the pressure build up in the nucleus after the unfolding of the folds implies a significant decrease in the NC ratio and a loss of nuclear scaling (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The number of free osmolytes in the nucleus decreases strongly during hypo-osmotic shock.
source: In reality, since free osmolytes are mainly accounted for by metabolites that are permeable to the nuclear envelope, the number of free osmolytes in the nucleus decreases strongly during the shock.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: The robustness of cell size scaling laws arises from three physical properties: electroneutrality, balance of water chemical potential, and balance of ionic fluxes.
source: Using a combination of physical arguments ranging from thermodynamics, statistical physics, polymer physics, mechanics, and electrostatics, we have provided evidence that the robustness of these scaling laws arises from three physical properties: electroneutrality, balance of water chemical potential, and balance of ionic fluxes.
evidence: This is the main theoretical conclusion of the study.

claim: The simplified Pump-Leak model focusing on leading order effects is a powerful way to isolate and better study the origin of the scaling laws.
source: The use of a simplified model focusing on the leading order effects, such as the homeostasis between amino acids and proteins, is a powerful way to isolate and better study the origin of the scaling laws.
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the approach used in the study.

claim: The dry mass dilution at senescence is believed to be of fundamental biological importance by establishing a functional relationship between cell size (and density) and cell senescence.
source: A phenomenon that was so far unexplained (Neurohr et al., 2019) despite the fact that it is believed to be of fundamental biological importance (Lengefeld et al., 2021) by establishing a functional relationship between cell size (and density) and cell senescence, potentially providing a new mechanism driving this important aging process.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Neurohr et al., 2019 and Lengefeld et al., 2021.

claim: The specific set of biological processes described in this article at the root of the variation of physical parameters is not ubiquitous.
source: We emphasize that while we claim that the physical laws and the coarse-grained physical parameters that constrain cell size are ubiquitous, the specific set of biological processes described in this article at the root of the variation of such parameters is not.
evidence: This is a clarification about the scope of the model's predictions.

claim: The saturation of DNA and mRNA is a new biological mechanism proposed to explain dry mass dilution at senescence.
source: In particular, the new biological mechanism, namely the saturation of DNA and mRNA, proposed here to explain dry mass dilution at senescence, is not the only biological mechanism that affects dry mass density.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the proposed mechanism.

claim: The large pool of metabolites is a robust feature throughout biology, making it one of the main causes of the universality of the cell size scaling laws observed in yeasts, bacteria, and mammalian cells.
source: Moreover, the large pool of metabolites is a robust feature throughout biology (Park et al., 2016), making it one of the main causes of the universality of the cell size scaling laws observed in yeasts, bacteria, and mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion supported by a citation to Park et al., 2016.

claim: The recent observation of the increase in diffusivities in the nucleus after blocking nuclear export is explained by the decoupling between protein and amino acid homeostasis after the impingement of ribosome synthesis.
source: For instance, the recent observation of the increase in diffusivities in the nucleus after blocking nuclear export is explained in our model by the decoupling between protein and amino acid homeostasis after the impingement of ribosome synthesis, a step that requires nuclear export (Lemière et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation of experimental observations cited from Lemière et al., 2022.

claim: The nuclear scaling originates from two features: the balance of osmotic pressures at the nuclear envelope and the presence of a large pool of metabolites.
source: As a consequence, we show that the nuclear scaling originates from two features. The first one is the balance of osmotic pressures at the nuclear envelope that we interpret as the result of the nonlinear elastic properties of the nucleus likely due to the presence of folds in the nuclear membrane of mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion from the nested Pump-Leak model.

claim: Yeast cells do not possess lamina such that the presence of nuclear folds may not be required for the scaling.
source: Interestingly, yeast cells do not possess lamina such that the presence of nuclear folds may not be required for the scaling.
evidence: This is a biological observation that qualifies the model's predictions.

claim: The osmotic pressure is balanced at the nuclear envelope in isotonic conditions.
source: In this regard, our model adds to a recently growing body of evidence suggesting that the osmotic pressure is balanced at the nuclear envelope in isotonic conditions (Deviri and Safran, 2022; Lemière et al., 2022; Finan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deviri and Safran, 2022, Lemière et al., 2022, and Finan et al., 2009.

claim: The genome size directly impacts the nuclear volume only if the number of (free) counterions of chromatin dominates the number of trapped proteins and the number of metabolites inside the nucleus.
source: Our results indicate that the genome size directly impacts the nuclear volume only if the number of (free) counterions of chromatin dominates the number of trapped proteins and the number of metabolites inside the nucleus.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion from the model.

claim: The number of chromatin counterions is comparable to the number of trapped proteins while it is about 60 times smaller than the number of metabolites.
source: We estimate that this number is comparable to the number of trapped proteins while it is about 60 times smaller than the number of metabolites.
evidence: This is based on order of magnitude estimates.

claim: Genome content does not directly determine nuclear volume.
source: This is in agreement with recent observations that genome content does not directly determine nuclear volume (Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cantwell and Nurse, 2019b.

claim: Genetic screen experiments done on fission yeast mutants support the prediction that gene expression affects nuclear volume through metabolism.
source: This prediction is in line with genetic screen experiments done on fission yeast mutants (Cantwell and Nurse, 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cantwell and Nurse, 2019a.

claim: For cells exhibiting high nuclear envelope potential such as some cancer cells, the number of metabolites in the nucleus directly depends on the chromatin content due to electrostatic effects.
source: However, when the chromatin charge is not diluted, which is likely to occur for cells exhibiting high nuclear envelope potential such as some cancer cells, our theory predicts that the number of metabolites in the nucleus also directly depends on the chromatin content due to electrostatic effects.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Chromatin charge is likely important in the nuclear-scaling breakdown in cancer.
source: This highlights the likely importance of chromatin charge in the nuclear-scaling breakdown in cancer.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation with potential biological implications.

claim: The nested Pump-Leak model predicts that the cell swells upon NEB if the nuclear envelope is under tension.
source: The nested Pump-Leak model predicts that the cell swells upon NEB if the nuclear envelope is under tension.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from the model.

claim: Artificially increasing the nuclear envelope tension through strong uniaxial cell confinement would synchronize mitotic swelling with NEB.
source: This prediction can be tested by artificially increasing the nuclear envelope tension through strong uniaxial cell confinement (Berre et al., 2014), which would synchronize mitotic swelling with NEB.
evidence: This is a testable prediction supported by a citation to Berre et al., 2014.

claim: Small osmolytes constitute the major part of the free osmolytes in a cell so that steric and short-range attractive interactions are only a small correction to the osmotic pressure.
source: The qualitative answer again comes from the fact that small osmolytes constitute the major part of the free osmolytes in a cell so that steric and short-range attractive interactions are only a small correction to the osmotic pressure.
evidence: This is a theoretical justification for the ideal solution approximation.

claim: The second virial coefficient gives a contribution to the osmotic pressure only of order 2 kPa, typically two orders of magnitude smaller than the ideal solution terms.
source: We confirm this point by estimating the second virial coefficient that gives a contribution to the osmotic pressure only of order 2 kPa (see Appendix 1, section 3.1), typically two orders of magnitude smaller than the ideal solution terms (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on order of magnitude estimates.

claim: Although the model uses an ideal gas law for the osmotic pressure, the Donnan equilibrium effectively accounts for the electrostatic interactions.
source: Moreover, we show in Appendix 1, section 7.1 that although we use an ideal gas law for the osmotic pressure, the Donnan equilibrium effectively accounts for the electrostatic interactions.
evidence: This is a theoretical justification presented in the Appendix.

claim: The theory can be generalized to take into account any ion species and ion transport law while keeping the same functional form for the expressions of the volume as long as only monovalent ions are considered.
source: Finally, our theory can be generalized to take into account any ions species and ion transport law while keeping the same functional form for the expressions of the volume (Equation A.21) as long as only monovalent ions are considered.
evidence: This is a statement about the generality of the theoretical framework.

claim: Multivalent ions such as calcium are in the micromolar range.
source: This is a very robust approximation because multivalent ions such as calcium are in the micromolar range.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: The framework can be used to explain the scaling of other membrane bound organelles such as vacuoles and mitochondria.
source: As a logical extension of our results, we suggest that our framework be used to explain the scaling of other membrane bound organelles such as vacuoles and mitochondria (Chan and Marshall, 2010).
evidence: This is a suggestion for future work supported by a citation to Chan and Marshall, 2010.

claim: The incorporation of other organelles into the framework leads to the same equations as for the nucleus, pointing out that the origin of the scaling of other organelles may also arise from the balance of osmotic pressures.
source: Provided that the organelles are constrained by the same physical laws, namely the balance of water chemical potential, the balance of ionic fluxes and the electroneutrality condition, we show in Appendix 1 (Equation A.83) that the incorporation of other organelles into our framework leads to the same equations as for the nucleus, thus pointing out that the origin of the scaling of other organelles may also arise from the balance of osmotic pressures.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction presented in the Appendix.

claim: The theory could be used to explain the scaling of membraneless organelles such as nucleoids.
source: We also propose that our theory be used to explain the scaling of membraneless organelles such as nucleoids (Gray et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a suggestion for future work supported by a citation to Gray et al., 2019.

claim: The Donnan picture does not require membranes.
source: Indeed, the Donnan picture that we are using does not require membranes (Barrat and Joanny, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Barrat and Joanny, 1996.

claim: Cell size scaling laws can be understood and predicted quantitatively on the basis of a remarkably simple set of physical laws ruling cell size as well as a simple set of universal biological features.
source: Taken as a whole, our study demonstrates that cell size scaling laws can be understood and predicted quantitatively on the basis of a remarkably simple set of physical laws ruling cell size as well as a simple set of universal biological features.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The theoretical framework is fundamental to cell biology and will likely benefit the large community of biologists working on cell size and growth.
source: The new interpretations of previous empirical biological phenomena that our approach allows to provide indicates that this theoretical framework is fundamental to cell biology and will likely benefit the large community of biologists working on cell size and growth.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance and potential impact of the work.
